definitions.gloss: buying a replacement; replacement purchase; upgrading
definitions.explanation: The act of purchasing a new item to replace an old or worn-out one. Common for appliances, electronics, cars, and other durable goods.

examples.japanese: パソコンの{買|か}い{替|か}えを{考|かんが}えている。
examples.english: I'm thinking about getting a new computer.

examples.japanese: {冷蔵庫|れいぞうこ}がそろそろ{買|か}い{替|か}えの{時期|じき}だ。
examples.english: It's about time to replace the refrigerator.

examples.japanese: {車|くるま}の{買|か}い{替|か}えには{補助金|ほじょきん}が{出|で}ることもある。
examples.english: There are sometimes subsidies available when replacing your car.

notes:
USAGE:
The noun form of the verb {買|か}い{替|か}える (to buy a replacement). Extremely common in consumer contexts — electronics, appliances, vehicles, and furniture. Often used with の{時期|じき} (time to replace).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {買|か}い{替|か}えの{時期|じき} (time for a replacement purchase)
- {買|か}い{替|か}えを{検討|けんとう}する (to consider replacing)
- {買|か}い{替|か}え{需要|じゅよう} (replacement demand)
- スマホの{買|か}い{替|か}え (replacing one's smartphone)
